papers.title: On the Stopping Distance and the Stopping Redundancy of Codes
papers.inspected_version: March2006 journal, pp.922-932; received17March2005, revised9December2005; preprint23March2005
papers.comparison: Matrix-dependent stopping distance and stopping redundancy differ. Codeword supports stop; changing redundant checks changes the graph. Their Theorem3 gives three for positive distinct columns, not the new four/six guarantees.

papers.title: Distance bounds for generalized bicycle codes
papers.comparison: Eq.8 uses HX=[A|B], HZT=[B;-A]. Our B=A-transpose. Eq.10 counts logical dimension via a gcd; it is not a stopping-distance theorem. No dimension formula is imported into our new proof.

papers.title: Degenerate quantum erasure decoding
papers.inspected_version: Article-in-press main PDF; accepted23February2026; published13March2026; version-of-record29April2026 metadata; first preprint20November2024
papers.comparison: Degenerate decoding can pass ordinary stopping obstructions. Performance/capacity claims concern a decoder and error model, not a lower stopping distance for our fixed HX. Introductory capacity questions are claimed answered within the paper.

papers.title: Stopping Sets in Codes from Designs
papers.inspected_version: Author manuscript reports original compositionSeptember2003 and ISIT2003 presentation; inspected undated revised web PDF
papers.comparison: Theorem1: uniform column weight w and distinct-column intersection at most mu give s>=w/mu+1. Here mu=2, hence three at w=4; our two-block refinement gives four. Corollary2 assumes intersection at most one, which fails across our blocks.
papers.archive_scope: Concatenated web-tool text snapshots, not original PDF bytes; original PDF download403.

scope: Four newly consulted accessible main texts, plus exact paper/version and search leads below. Historical claims remain historical; broad directions are not counted as precise targets.

excluded_or_resolved_passages.outcome: Etzion resolves the extended-Hamming instance positively and disproves optimality of the first-order RM construction. Han-Siegel upper-bound improvements already appear here.
Two capacity/linear-decoding questions are explicitly claimed answered by this same paper; not harvested as still-open questions.
The tempting divisibility conjecture is explicitly refuted, and both small-plane enumerators are completed later in the same manuscript.
